subject: Network topology validation for private deployment (control plane / data plane)
messages:
From: Maria Borges <maria.borges@acme-retail.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: acme-networking@acme-retail.com
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial network sketch for Redwood private deployment

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier this week. Attached is a starter sketch from our network team showing how they'd like to carve subnets for control-plane endpoints (private control API, metrics collector) vs. data-plane GPU clusters. High-level asks from Acme:

- Keep control plane ingress limited to our management VPC via a set of private endpoints (no public internet).
- Allow data-plane agents to fetch model artifacts from Redwood S3-compatible origin via an egress proxy with mTLS.
- Ensure that telemetry and trace collection don't traverse public internet; prefer VPC peering or Transit Gateway + route table controls.

We included NAT gateway vs. egress proxy options in acme-proposed-segmentation.xlsx. Can your infra team validate the constraints (ports, healthcheck requirements, certificate rotation expectations) and confirm any required edge components on Redwood's side?

Appreciate it — Maria
Network Ops, Acme Retail

--- Attachment stubs: redwood-vpc-refarch-v1.pdf (diagram), acme-proposed-segmentation.xlsx (sheet)
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Maria Borges <maria.borges@acme-retail.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial network sketch for Redwood private deployment

Thanks Maria — tagging Karthik and Hannah for infra/security detail review. Initial notes from my side:

- Separation of control-plane (management API, rollout API, audit endpoints) and data-plane (worker nodes, model serving) is a good call. We recommend two distinct peering constructs:
  * Control-plane: Private endpoint in Acme VPC -> peered to Redwood control VPC (no public IPs).
  * Data-plane: Dedicated VPC/VPN for GPU hosts with controlled egress to a Redwood managed egress proxy.

- Certificate rotation: Redwood expects 3rd-party mTLS rotation every 90 days; we can support ACME-style automated rotation if you prefer.
- Healthchecks: control-plane requires outbound HTTPS (443) from our control plane into your management CIDR for callback webhooks and agent heartbeats (we'll restrict to a small port set).

I'll let Karthik share the exact port/port-range and Hannah confirm logging/audit flow. Also attaching the brief ref-arch so we have a common image.

Best,
Irene
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference

--- Attachment: redwood-vpc-refarch-v1.pdf (diagram)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Maria Borges <maria.borges@acme-retail.com>
Cc: david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 08:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial network sketch for Redwood private deployment

Maria — quick technical confirmation and a small ask from infra:

- Control plane ports: HTTPS (443) for API endpoints. Websocket/streaming uses 443 over TLS as well. No additional ports required if you allow SNI-based routing.
- Data plane artifact pulls: outbound HTTPS (443) to our artifact origin (we will provide a private endpoint FQDN that resolves over peering).
- Healthchecks: TCP 9443 + HTTPS 443 for agent diagnostics (we can collapse to 443, but some internal agent agents expose a diagnostics port for local tooling; this is optional).
- Egress options: NAT Gateway vs. Egress proxy (Envoy): if you want consistent mTLS and egress policy we recommend the Envoy egress proxy pattern (we can supply a Helm chart for the agent).

Operational constraints: please ensure the data-plane subnets can support jumbo-mounted ephemeral disks and MTU 9001 across the peering/Transit path if you intend GPU instance types with RDMA. If not, we can downsize to MTU 1500 and adjust kernel setting in the agent image.

David — can you run a short tcpflow test from a representative GPU host and attach results?

-karthik
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Maria Borges <maria.borges@acme-retail.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 14:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial network sketch for Redwood private deployment

Attached tcpflow-test-results-20270412.log — ran from a c5g-like instance in a demo data-plane VPC towards the proposed artifact endpoint. Observations:

- TLS handshake completes with the Redwood origin certificate signed by our CA.
- Time-to-first-byte averaged 42ms (us-west region), stable under light load.
- If Acme will use MTU 9001 for RoCE/RDMA GPU instances, we observed packet fragmentation via an intermediate NAT gateway in our lab (need straight peering/Transit without NAT for RDMA).

Action items from infra:
- If you plan RDMA, Acme must provide a non-NAT path (Transit Gateway peering or direct connect equivalent).
- Provide a CIDR range for control-plane endpoint allowlist (we'll produce a short-lived list with rotation).

- Attachment: tcpflow-test-results-20270412.log

-David
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Maria Borges <maria.borges@acme-retail.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 10:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial network sketch for Redwood private deployment

Maria — a couple compliance/observability notes:

- Audit logs: control-plane audit events will be pushed to your log collector over a private forwarder (TLS + mTLS). We will not send audit events over public endpoints. Need to confirm max QPS for event delivery; default is 250 ev/sec per control-plane endpoint (we can throttle).
- Tracing: we can sample at 1% by default across the data-plane; if you want full-trace for onboarding, we recommend staging for 48 hours with sampling bumped to 10%.
- Packet capture: we discourage customer-side packet capture inside encrypted tunnels; if Acme needs wire-level capture for debugging, coordinate a short maintenance window so we can enable debug mode on the egress proxy.

Security ask: please confirm whether Acme intends to manage its own PKI (preferred) or have Redwood-managed certs for the private endpoints. If Acme manages PKI, we'll accept signed cert bundles via the enrollment API.

Thanks,
Hannah
Staff Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Maria Borges <maria.borges@acme-retail.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Apr 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial network sketch for Redwood private deployment

Maria — thanks for the quick responses and the topology sketch. Summary & next steps (agree/please correct if I misrepresent anything):

1) Architecture decisions (agreed):
   - Control plane: private endpoint peered into Acme management VPC; only HTTPS (443) inbound from Redwood for callbacks; audit events forwarded over a private TLS channel.
   - Data plane: dedicated VPC for GPU hosts peered via Transit Gateway; no NAT in path if Acme requires RDMA (MTU 9001). Otherwise we will default to MTU 1500 and use an Envoy egress proxy for mTLS artifact pulls.
2) Certificates & PKI:
   - Acme to confirm PKI choice by 2027-04-22 (manage own PKI or Redwood-managed). If self-managed, send CSR + chain via the enrollment API (we'll provide a shortened window).
3) Operational items for Acme:
   - Share control-plane allowlist CIDRs by 2027-04-20.
   - Confirm whether Transit Gateway or Direct Connect will be used for RDMA traffic.
4) Action owners & ETA:
   - Karthik: produce exact port list + egress proxy helm chart (ETA 4/19).
   - David: provide final artifact FQDN + any S3 origin ACL needs (ETA 4/18).
   - Hannah: integration checklist for audit-trace collection and desired sampling windows (ETA 4/20).

Please reply with a quick ACK or any changes; if we get confirmations above, we'll schedule a joint test window the week of 4/26 to validate connectivity and end-to-end artifact pulls.

Best,
Irene Choi
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
